correctness.rationale: Success at the right endpoint requires positive final velocity and hence even parity from the inward positive start. In rate-scaled length, first-flight conditioning gives the marked backward equations; eliminating the minus component yields f_+''=(1−z²)f_+, f_+'(0)=f_+(0), f_+(c)=1. Thus the marked boundary value is 1/F_c(1−z²), in particular 1/(1+c) at z=1. Absorption occurs almost surely because at each flight the chance of an exit without another reversal is at least e^(−c). The entire function F_c(s) is the value at c of the scalar solution with u(0)=u'(0)=1; at a zero, integration by parts gives −s=(∫|u'|²+|u(0)|²)/∫|u|²>0. With ξ=c√(−s) the root equation is tan ξ=−ξ/c, one simple root in each stated half-period, none at zero. Growth at most exp(O(√|s|)) and ∑ξ_n^(−2)<∞ justify the normalized genus-zero product, with no exponential linear factor. Its ratios give the stated geometrics; the sum of their means is finite. The absolutely convergent log series gives the positive Lévy masses and rate −log H_c(0); F_c(1)=e^c. Independently expanding the two coefficients at s=0 gives Var(M)=A+A²−2B for A=F_c'(0)/F_c(0), B=F_c''(0)/(2F_c(0)); the factored expression and mean and variance scaling were checked by exact algebra. The supplied checker checks simulated success, mean and mass at zero, not simulated variance. At s>0 the Laplace limit follows by substituting q=e^(−s/c²), and at s=0 the transforms equal one. Euler's product and the convergent inverse squares and fourth powers give the independent-exponential law and its moments. These checks establish correctness without asserting physical-time or path convergence.
residual_risks: The statements concern counts under right-exit conditioning, not physical crossing time or other boundary conditions. Finite simulations in the frozen record are not relied on for tail laws, the product or variance.

evidence: At s=0 the numerator is 1 and the denominator is F_c(1−q). F_c(t) is the value at c of u''=tu, u(0)=u'(0)=1; the standard self-adjoint Robin–Dirichlet problem gives simple roots −ξ_n²/c² and F_c has order at most 1/2. The genus-zero product divided by its value at t=0 then gives factors r_n²/(r_n²+1−q).

Each factor has log ∑_{k≥1}(q^k−1)(1+r_n²)^(−k)/k, and −log H_c(0)=c−log(1+c). The moments and q=e^(−s/c²) limit are direct operations on the available function; Euler's product for sinh identifies the limit.
